summary: Intermittent p99 latency and capacity shortfall from long-lived low-throughput sessions holding HBM reservations; autoscaler heartbeat misread
description: Issue summary: Customer on a Dedicated pool is seeing intermittent p99 latency spikes and dropped throughput during sustained low-QPS workloads. Impact: Customer reports 20-35% throughput reduction across pinned routes during two daily windows. Environment: prod us-east-1 dedicated pool assigned to DocuSense (reserved capacity).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Route steady low QPS traffic with long-lived streaming sessions (keepalives every 60s) to the dedicated pool. 2) Maintain a handful (10-30) of long-lived sessions with occasional 1-2 token heartbeats. 3) Observe attach times and allocator HBM reservations during the window. Expected: stable attach and autoscale behavior; Observed: prolonged attach, P99 spikes, autoscaler failing to add slots in time.
logs: Relevant traces pulled from grafana: grafana.redwood/internal/dashboards/attach-latency?from=2026-03-09T08:00Z&to=2026-03-10T20:00Z; example error: "slot attach wait > 12s" repeated; allocator logs show repeated HBM reservation entries and delayed lease returns. Metric snapshot: attach_time.p99 spike to 9.8s, pool_alloc_free_slots down by 30% during event windows.
investigation_notes: Initial triage (2026-03-10): Observed correlation between long-lived sessions and HBM reserved memory not released promptly after session idle periods. Hypothesis A: long-lived sessions are holding small persistent KV caches and HBM reservations that block slot reuse leading to effective capacity shrink. Hypothesis B: autoscaler heartbeat aggregator misinterprets low QPS heartbeats as healthy and avoids scaling while attach queue grows. Evidence: allocator debug shows 'reserve_hbm' artifacts tied to session IDs with long TTLs; autoscaler logs show heartbeat from those sessions classified as 'steady' because of keepalive, preventing predictive scale-up.
comments: Support - Ava Martinez (2026-03-10): Customer reported initial spike at 08:45 UTC. Collected traces and asked customer for client-side keepalive pattern. Requested vpc/tenant identifiers.

SRE - Samir Patel (2026-03-10): Pulled allocator debug logs and increased attach tracing for the pool. Noted HBM reservations with TTL 24h attached to session tokens. Added a temporary metric to track long-lived-session-count.

Customer - DocuSense Ops (2026-03-11): Confirmed they use long-lived streaming sessions for user presence; keepalive interval is 60s and sometimes sends 1-byte heartbeats. Will test with shorter TTLs and report.

SRE - Samir Patel (2026-03-11): Ran controlled repro in staging. Reproduced p99 attach spikes when 20+ sessions held HBM with infrequent activity. Applied a temporary mitigation on pool: reduced session HBM TTLs to 5m for new attaches to allow faster reclamation. Observed attach p99 drop ~60% after mitigation.

Engineering - Priya Rao (2026-03-12): Investigating autoscaler classifier logic. Found a condition where keepalive-only sessions were counted as low-utilization stable instead of idle, preventing scaling triggers. Drafting PR to change classifier to treat heartbeat-only sessions as 'idle' for predictive scaling decisions.

Support - Ava Martinez (2026-03-12): Communicated mitigation to customer and scheduled a follow-up test window. Customer agreed to a client-side change to reduce keepalive frequency and add session expiry during off-hours.
resolution: Mitigation applied: temporarily reduced HBM reservation TTL for new attaches in affected pool (2026-03-11) which recovered attach P99 by ~60%. Engineering PR (#2679) created to update autoscaler classifier to treat heartbeat-only sessions as idle; PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/2679. Customer to deploy client change to session expiry and reduced keepalive frequency. Next steps: 1) Roll PR to canary on prod by 2026-03-15. 2) Monitor for recurrence across other dedicated pools. 3) Add a dashboard tile for long-lived-session HBM reservations and a paging alert when count > 10 per pool.
follow_up_tasks: Roll autoscaler classifier PR to canary and validate during peak window
Add alert: long_lived_session_hbm_count > 10 triggers P1 triage
Update runbook to include guidance for clients using long-lived streams (recommended keepalive patterns)
